description: The Terminal Three, led by Shreejit Podder, is a team passionate about coding, AI, space science, and innovation. We aim to solve real-world challenges through creativity and technology. We welcome motivated beginners and experienced participants. We are looking for teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, web development, data analysis, physics, UI/UX design, and scientific research.
summary:
FLAREX (Fire Learning and Research Explorer) is an AI-assisted interactive platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, understand, and compare.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity than on Earth. Changes in flame behavior, heat transfer, and combustion products create unique fire-safety challenges for spacecraft, lunar habitats, and future Mars missions. However, information from different space-based combustion investigations can be difficult to locate and compare.

FLAREX addresses this challenge by organizing research information from NASA investigations such as BASS, Saffire, ACME, FLEX, SAME, and SoFIE. Users can explore experiment objectives, fuel types, environmental conditions, sensors, measurement methods, and documented findings through an organized research dashboard.

The platform aims to provide interactive investigation comparisons, scientific data visualizations, AI-assisted explanations, and research-gap identification. It also distinguishes verified experimental findings from general descriptions and interpretations to maintain scientific accuracy.

By transforming scattered research information into an accessible and structured experience, FLAREX aims to help students and researchers better understand combustion in microgravity and support the development of safer systems for future human space exploration.
details:
1. The Problem We Address

FLAREX

Fire Learning and Research Explorer

Turning Microgravity Combustion Data into Space Fire Safety Insights

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Challenge: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
Project Type: AI-Assisted Scientific Research and Data Analysis Platform
Developer: Independent Student Developer
Platform: Web-Based Scientific Research Application

1. Executive Summary

FLAREX (Fire Learning and Research Explorer) is an AI-assisted scientific research and data exploration platform designed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible, structured, understandable, and analyzable.

Fire is one of the most important safety concerns in human spaceflight. Combustion in microgravity can behave differently from combustion under normal terrestrial gravity. The absence of ordinary buoyancy-driven convection changes how flames develop, how heat and combustion products move, and how researchers observe flame behavior. These differences make understanding combustion in spacecraft environments particularly important.

Over several decades, space agencies and research institutions have conducted numerous experiments to investigate flame behavior, material flammability, soot formation, smoke particles, droplet combustion, airflow effects, and fire behavior in spacecraft-like environments.

However, scientific knowledge about these experiments is distributed across research publications, investigation records, technical reports, scientific databases, and experimental datasets. Finding relevant studies, understanding their experimental conditions, comparing their findings, and identifying gaps in available evidence can require substantial time and technical knowledge.

FLAREX addresses this challenge by providing a centralized scientific research environment.

The platform combines structured research metadata, scientific source references, dataset ingestion, statistical analysis, cross-study comparison, evidence classification, research-gap identification, reproducibility tracking, and AI-assisted research synthesis.

Rather than treating AI-generated explanations as scientific facts, FLAREX separates documented source information, published experimental findings, independently calculated statistics, and AI-generated interpretations.

Its primary objective is to help users explore the scientific knowledge surrounding microgravity combustion while making the research process more transparent, reproducible, and understandable.

FLAREX is an independent student-developed research platform. It is not an official NASA system and does not replace certified spacecraft fire-safety equipment or engineering procedures.

2. The Scientific Problem

2.1 Why Fire Behaves Differently in Space

On Earth, gravity plays an important role in combustion through buoyancy-driven convection.

When a flame heats the surrounding gas, the hot gas becomes less dense and rises. Cooler air moves toward the flame, creating a circulation pattern that influences flame shape, oxygen transport, heat transfer, and combustion-product movement.

In microgravity, this familiar buoyancy-driven circulation is greatly reduced.

Consequently, several aspects of combustion can change:

  • Flame shape and structure may differ from terrestrial flames.
  • Heat and combustion products may move differently.
  • Oxygen transport can become more dependent on diffusion and imposed airflow.
  • Soot formation and oxidation behavior can change.
  • Flame stability can depend strongly on the surrounding environment.
  • Smoke particles may have different transport and deposition behavior.
  • Material geometry and environmental conditions can influence combustion in ways that are difficult to predict from ordinary Earth-based observations.

These differences make microgravity combustion a distinct scientific research area.

2.2 Why Spacecraft Fire Safety Requires Research

A spacecraft is a controlled environment where people depend on life-support systems, electrical equipment, enclosed structures, and carefully selected materials.

Understanding fire behavior in such environments requires knowledge of several interconnected scientific areas:

Combustion behavior: How flames develop, spread, stabilize, and interact with their surroundings.

Material behavior: How different solid materials respond to heating and combustion conditions.

Smoke and particle formation: How combustion produces particles and how these particles behave in reduced-gravity environments.

Environmental conditions: How oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, temperature, and geometry influence experimental outcomes.

Fire detection research: How changes in flame and smoke behavior affect the interpretation of experimental observations.

Research in these areas helps scientists improve their understanding of potential fire-related hazards in spacecraft environments.

FLAREX focuses on organizing and exploring this scientific knowledge. It does not claim to independently certify materials, predict operational spacecraft fire events, or determine safe engineering limits.

2.3 The Research Accessibility Problem

A major challenge is not simply the lack of scientific research. A significant challenge is the difficulty of accessing and connecting the research that already exists.

Relevant information can be distributed across:

  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI).
  • NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS).
  • Scientific journal publications.
  • Experimental investigation descriptions.
  • Research presentations and technical documents.
  • Publicly available scientific datasets.

These resources may use different terminology, measurement units, experimental configurations, and documentation formats.

For a student or researcher, comparing two investigations can require manually reviewing multiple documents and identifying which experimental conditions are actually comparable.

FLAREX attempts to reduce this complexity through a unified research interface.

3. Project Objectives

FLAREX was developed around several major objectives.

Objective 1: Centralize Scientific Research Information

Create a structured environment for exploring relevant microgravity combustion investigations and their associated scientific references.

Objective 2: Improve Research Accessibility

Allow users to discover investigations, examine their research context, understand available evidence, and navigate source references.

Objective 3: Enable Scientific Dataset Analysis

Provide tools for importing available datasets and performing descriptive statistical analysis without requiring users to build an independent analysis environment.

Objective 4: Support Cross-Study Comparison

Help users compare experimental conditions and understand when two investigations are compatible, partially comparable, or fundamentally different.

Objective 5: Introduce Evidence-Based AI Assistance

Use AI to assist with research questions and scientific explanations while maintaining source references and clearly distinguishing interpretations from experimental findings.

Objective 6: Identify Research Gaps

Highlight missing information, incomplete evidence, unavailable measurements, and opportunities for further scientific investigation.

Objective 7: Improve Reproducibility

Record analysis parameters, dataset identifiers, software information, and processing methods so that analytical results can be examined and reproduced.

4. The FLAREX Solution

FLAREX is designed as an integrated scientific research platform rather than a simple collection of research links.

It brings together multiple research workflows within a single web application.

The platform follows a structured process:

Discover → Retrieve → Organize → Validate → Analyze → Compare → Interpret → Report

Each stage contributes to the overall research process.

4.1 Scientific Investigation Explorer

The Investigation Explorer provides a centralized interface for browsing documented combustion-related investigations.

Users can explore research records, examine their scientific objectives, review experimental context, and navigate associated publications or source references.

The research database contains curated metadata covering investigations and research areas such as:

  • BASS-II.
  • Saffire investigations.
  • SAME and SAME-R.
  • FLEX and FLEX-2 investigations.
  • ACME investigations.
  • DAFT.
  • SLICE.
  • SPICE.
  • Confined Combustion.
  • SoFIE-OFFS.
  • SoFIE-MIST.
  • Relevant solid-fuel combustion research.
  • Complementary terrestrial battery research.

These records provide a structured starting point for scientific exploration.

An important distinction is maintained: a research record does not automatically mean that its complete experimental dataset is available within FLAREX.

4.2 Investigation Details

Each investigation can be examined through a structured scientific profile.

Depending on available source information, the profile can include:

  • Investigation name and identification.
  • Scientific objectives.
  • Research background.
  • Experimental materials.
  • Experimental environment.
  • Environmental variables.
  • Measurement methods.
  • Sensors and instrumentation.
  • Published findings.
  • Supporting references.
  • Evidence classification.
  • Known limitations.
  • Missing information.

This structure helps users understand not only what an experiment investigated, but also what information is actually documented.

4.3 Scientific Data Explorer

The Scientific Data Explorer is designed to help users work with available numerical datasets.

Supported import formats include:

  • CSV.
  • TSV.
  • TXT.
  • JSON.

After importing a dataset, the system can inspect its structure and identify relevant analytical fields.

The processing workflow includes:

  1. File parsing.
  2. Column identification.
  3. Variable and unit extraction where possible.
  4. Missing-value identification.
  5. Duplicate-row detection.
  6. Non-numeric value identification.
  7. Data validation.
  8. Statistical processing.
  9. Visualization.
  10. Export of analytical results.

The system preserves the original imported records separately from normalized analytical representations.

Missing or corrupted values are not silently converted into scientifically meaningful measurements.

This is important because incorrect data handling can produce misleading statistical results.

Available Statistical Analysis

The reported analytical capabilities include:

  • Sample count.
  • Missing-value percentage.
  • Mean.
  • Median.
  • Minimum.
  • Maximum.
  • Sample standard deviation.
  • Histograms.
  • Pearson correlation.
  • Spearman correlation.
  • Ordinary Least Squares regression.
  • Moving averages.
  • Sequence and time-series summaries.

The system also provides visual exploration through charts such as histograms, scatter plots, and line charts.

However, these statistical functions do not automatically establish scientific causation.

For example, a correlation between two variables does not prove that one variable causes a change in the other.

All statistical results must be interpreted in the context of the experimental design, measurement methods, and source dataset.

4.4 Investigation Comparison Engine

Different combustion investigations may examine related scientific questions while using different experimental conditions.

For example, two studies might investigate flame behavior but use different:

  • Gravity environments.
  • Oxygen concentrations.
  • Pressures.
  • Airflow conditions.
  • Fuel types.
  • Material geometries.
  • Measurement techniques.
  • Temperature ranges.

Directly combining their numerical results without considering these differences can produce misleading conclusions.

FLAREX includes an Experimental Condition Intelligence system designed to examine these dimensions.

Its comparison framework considers:

  1. Gravity environment.
  2. Pressure.
  3. Oxygen concentration.
  4. Airflow.
  5. Fuel or material.
  6. Temperature.
  7. Experimental geometry.
  8. Measurement methods.
  9. Additional experimental metadata.

The system classifies comparisons into categories such as:

  • Compatible.
  • Partially comparable.
  • Incompatible.
  • Missing information.

This helps users understand whether two studies can reasonably be compared.

A compatibility label is an analytical aid, not proof that two experiments are scientifically equivalent.

5. Evidence Intelligence System

One of FLAREX's central design principles is scientific evidence transparency.

Scientific information can come from different types of sources, and those sources do not all provide the same level of evidence.

For example, a peer-reviewed experimental paper may contain measurements and documented findings, while an investigation overview may only describe the purpose and general setup of an experiment.

FLAREX's Evidence Intelligence system organizes information according to its evidence type.

The reported evidence categories include:

  1. Direct experimental evidence.
  2. Published research findings.
  3. Derived statistical results.
  4. Supporting scientific literature.
  5. Investigation descriptions.
  6. Secondary research summaries.
  7. AI-generated interpretations.

The system is intended to prevent users from confusing an explanation generated by AI with a result directly measured during an experiment.

5.1 Claim Citation Verification

Scientific claims should be connected to relevant sources.

FLAREX includes a Claim Citation Verifier designed to classify citation and evidence states.

The system distinguishes between situations such as:

  • A claim supported by an original source.
  • A claim supported by retrieved metadata.
  • A claim with an available publication but incomplete verification.
  • A claim requiring manual review.
  • A claim with unavailable supporting information.
  • A claim that cannot currently be verified.

This approach makes it easier to identify unsupported or weakly supported statements.

5.2 Scientific Conflict and Uncertainty Detection

Research studies do not always produce identical findings.

Differences can result from experimental conditions, materials, measurement methods, sample sizes, or other factors.

FLAREX includes a Scientific Conflict and Uncertainty Detector designed to highlight:

  • Conflicting research statements.
  • Inconsistent experimental conditions.
  • Missing measurement information.
  • Differences in methodology.
  • Uncertain source relationships.
  • Potentially incompatible numerical comparisons.

The purpose is not to force all studies into one conclusion.

Instead, the system encourages users to recognize uncertainty and examine the underlying evidence.

6. AI Research Assistant

FLAREX integrates AI-assisted scientific research functionality using the Google Gemini API.

The AI Research Assistant is designed to help users understand research information, explore scientific questions, and navigate the platform's structured research records.

It is not intended to replace scientific publications or independently establish experimental facts.

6.1 Grounded Research Mode

This mode focuses on answering questions using relevant research records and available source references.

The system retrieves relevant information, prepares a focused context, and generates an explanation.

Where available, answers are associated with source references.

If the database does not contain enough information to answer a question, the assistant should communicate that limitation rather than inventing experimental findings.

6.2 Document Analysis Mode

This mode is intended to support the examination of imported scientific documents and their contents.

Users can use it to understand research terminology, identify important information, and organize scientific observations.

AI-generated explanations must remain distinguishable from the original document's statements.

6.3 Local Research Brief Mode

This mode provides a research summary using locally available project information.

It is particularly useful when external AI services are unavailable or when a user wants to explore the curated research database without depending on a live model response.

6.4 Retrieval-Augmented Generation

FLAREX uses a retrieval-oriented approach to reduce irrelevant AI responses.

The reported retrieval workflow includes:

  1. Query normalization.
  2. Query classification.
  3. Relevant record retrieval.
  4. Relevance scoring.
  5. Context selection.
  6. Evidence inspection.
  7. Citation validation.
  8. Response generation.

The system also provides retrieval diagnostics to help inspect why certain records were selected or excluded.

6.5 AI Reliability and Transparency

AI systems can produce inaccurate or unsupported information.

FLAREX therefore includes reliability-oriented features such as:

  • Source-grounded context.
  • Citation checks.
  • Evidence classification.
  • Missing-evidence warnings.
  • Request cancellation.
  • Error handling.
  • Retry logic.
  • Local research fallback.
  • Explicit separation of scientific findings and AI interpretations.

Gemini availability can vary, and API timeouts have been reported during development.

For this reason, FLAREX does not claim that every AI response is guaranteed to be correct or that the external AI service is always available.

7. NASA Scientific Data Discovery and Source Integration

FLAREX is designed to connect scientific research records with relevant public scientific resources.

Its reported integrations include NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics repository and NASA Technical Reports Server.

7.1 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics

The NASA PSI repository provides access to research information associated with physical sciences investigations.

FLAREX includes a source discovery workflow designed to inspect publicly accessible PSI resources and identify available research materials.

The project also inspected NASA's public PSI AWS mirror.

The inspection identified public prefixes including:

  • DSI.
  • OASIS.
  • pk4.

However, the inspected public mirror did not provide the required combustion telemetry CSV files.

Therefore, the project does not claim to have downloaded or analyzed unavailable raw experimental telemetry from that mirror.

Authenticated or interactive portal downloads may require separate manual access and verification.

7.2 NASA Technical Reports Server

NASA NTRS provides access to NASA technical publications and research reports.

FLAREX includes NTRS-related functionality for retrieving publication metadata and available document content.

Two relevant research references include:

BASS-II: NASA NTRS record 20160000593.

Saffire: NASA NTRS record 20180005168.

The platform uses source availability states to distinguish between metadata retrieval, document retrieval, file validation, and successful data ingestion.

An HTTP success response alone is not treated as proof that a scientific dataset has been retrieved or validated.

7.3 Source Transparency

FLAREX uses a multi-stage source availability model.

The reported source classification includes states such as:

  • Original source verified.
  • Metadata retrieved.
  • File successfully retrieved.
  • File structure validated.
  • Data successfully imported.
  • Link not checked.
  • Requires manual review.
  • Source unavailable.

These states help users understand exactly how far the platform has progressed with a source.

This is particularly important when working with scientific repositories where a publication, dataset record, downloadable file, and validated numerical dataset are different things.

8. Research Gap Explorer

Scientific research is not only about identifying what is already known.

It is also about identifying what remains unknown.

The FLAREX Research Gap Explorer is designed to highlight missing evidence and incomplete research coverage.

It examines research records and available metadata to identify areas where information is incomplete or where comparisons are difficult.

Potential research gaps include:

  • Missing numerical experimental data.
  • Incomplete experimental conditions.
  • Limited measurement details.
  • Missing sensor information.
  • Unavailable source documents.
  • Incomplete documentation of environmental variables.
  • Lack of directly comparable experiments.
  • Limited evidence connecting different research areas.

For example, two investigations might both examine combustion behavior but provide different levels of information about airflow, pressure, oxygen concentration, or measurement techniques.

The Research Gap Explorer can help highlight these missing fields.

These outputs should be interpreted as research opportunities or documentation gaps, not proof that no research exists anywhere.

9. Reproducible Scientific Computing

Scientific analysis should be traceable.

A numerical result is more useful when researchers can identify which dataset was used, which variables were selected, and which analytical method produced the result.

FLAREX includes a Reproducibility Ledger designed to record important information about analytical runs.

The reported ledger includes:

  • Run identifier.
  • Dataset identifier.
  • Source version.
  • Selected variables.
  • Measurement units.
  • Analytical method.
  • Sample count.
  • Missing-value handling.
  • Software version.
  • Execution timestamp.
  • Dataset checksum where available.

The platform also uses SHA-256 checksums to support dataset identity and integrity tracking.

This helps users distinguish between different versions of a dataset and provides a record of the analytical process.

The objective is to make the research workflow more transparent and easier to reproduce.

10. Scientific Audit Center

FLAREX includes a Scientific Audit Center designed to review the quality and completeness of research information.

The reported platform includes a multi-category scientific audit framework.

Its intended responsibilities include:

  • Source availability inspection.
  • Citation verification.
  • Evidence classification.
  • Dataset structure validation.
  • Missing-value analysis.
  • Duplicate detection.
  • Measurement-unit inspection.
  • Experimental condition completeness.
  • Statistical method tracking.
  • Reproducibility checks.
  • Research limitation reporting.
  • AI-generated interpretation separation.
  • Scientific claim verification.
  • Overall research transparency.

The audit system is intended to help users identify weaknesses before interpreting or reporting scientific results.

It does not constitute independent peer review, laboratory validation, or certification by a scientific authority.

11. Publication Studio

Scientific findings are more useful when they can be communicated clearly.

FLAREX includes a Publication Studio designed to generate structured research reports.

The reported system supports different report types and separates different categories of information.

The main information layers include:

SOURCE_FACT: Information directly documented by an identified source.

PUBLISHED_RESULT: Findings reported in a scientific publication.

DERIVED_STATISTICS: Results calculated from imported data using documented methods.

AI_INTERPRETATION: AI-generated explanations or interpretations.

This separation is intended to reduce the risk of presenting an AI-generated statement as an experimentally established result.

The reported export formats include:

  • Markdown.
  • JSON.
  • CSV.
  • Print-to-PDF.

Reports can include source information, methods, statistical summaries, limitations, and analytical context.

12. Technical Architecture

FLAREX is built as a web-based application using a modern frontend and backend architecture.

Frontend

React: Provides the component-based user interface.

TypeScript: Adds static typing and improves maintainability.

Recharts: Supports scientific data visualization.

The interface follows a dark aerospace-inspired design system, with a responsive layout for desktop and mobile screens.

Backend

Node.js: Provides the JavaScript runtime.

Express.js: Handles backend routes, API requests, and server-side processing.

The backend is responsible for operations that should not be exposed directly in the browser, including AI API communication and source-related requests.

AI Integration

Google Gemini API: Provides AI-assisted research explanations and synthesis.

The API key is intended to remain on the server side rather than being exposed in frontend code.

Data Processing

The platform uses JavaScript-based data processing for:

  • Dataset parsing.
  • Data validation.
  • Statistical calculations.
  • Research retrieval.
  • Evidence organization.
  • Comparison.
  • Reproducibility records.

Visualization

Charts and graphical representations help users explore available data and understand analytical outputs.

The system should only display scientific numerical charts when suitable numerical data is actually available.

A research metadata record must not be treated as an experimental measurement dataset.

13. User Interface and Experience

FLAREX uses a dark aerospace-inspired interface designed to make a complex scientific research workflow easier to navigate.

The reported application includes 14 views across its architecture.

Major areas include:

  1. Dashboard.
  2. Investigation Explorer.
  3. Investigation Details.
  4. Investigation Comparison.
  5. Scientific Data Explorer.
  6. Data Workbench.
  7. Evidence Intelligence.
  8. Research Gap Explorer.
  9. AI Research Assistant.
  10. Knowledge Graph.
  11. Sources and References.
  12. Scientific Audit Center.
  13. Workspace.
  14. Publication Studio.

The dashboard provides an overview of research coverage, available records, and system status.

The investigation explorer helps users discover research.

The data workbench provides tools for importing and analyzing available datasets.

The evidence and audit modules support scientific transparency.

The workspace and publication tools help organize and communicate research outputs.

The application is designed to be responsive across desktop and mobile screen sizes.

14. Knowledge Graph

FLAREX includes a Knowledge Graph designed to represent relationships between investigations, research materials, measurements, sources, and findings.

The reported graph architecture includes relationship types such as:

  • INVESTIGATES.
  • USES_MATERIAL.
  • MEASURES.
  • USES_SENSOR.
  • DOCUMENTED_IN.
  • SUPPORTS_FINDING.
  • RELATED_TO.

Additional relationship types were introduced in later development stages.

The graph can help users explore connections between different investigations and research topics.

For example, users may explore which investigations examine similar materials, which measurement methods are associated with particular research areas, and which sources document a particular finding.

The graph distinguishes verified relationships from inferred relationships.

This is important because a relationship suggested by metadata or AI should not automatically be treated as a directly documented scientific connection.

15. Development and Validation

FLAREX was developed through multiple iterative software development and testing stages.

The platform progressed through successive versions, with each stage adding research, analysis, validation, and transparency features.

According to the latest implementation report, FLAREX 7.0 includes:

  • 14 integrated application views.
  • A 16-record curated research database.
  • A scientific data ingestion system.
  • Evidence intelligence.
  • Source transparency.
  • Cross-study comparison.
  • Statistical analysis.
  • Reproducibility tracking.
  • Scientific audit functionality.
  • AI research assistance.
  • Research reporting and export.

15.1 Automated Testing

The latest reported automated test result is:

61/61 tests passed.

The implementation report also states:

  • TypeScript checks completed without errors.
  • Production build completed successfully.
  • Browser testing was performed on desktop and mobile layouts.
  • No browser console errors or warnings were reported during the described test sessions.
  • No horizontal overflow was reported in the tested mobile layout.

These are development-reported results, not independent third-party certification.

15.2 Large Dataset Processing

The system includes a chunked processing approach using Web Workers.

A dataset containing 50,051 rows was tested through the reported unit-testing workflow.

However, a full browser-based upload and end-to-end processing test of datasets exceeding 50,000 rows was not independently completed.

This distinction is maintained in the project's validation documentation.

15.3 External Service Testing

The project includes NASA-related source discovery and NTRS retrieval functionality.

However, the following limitations remain:

  • Authenticated PSI portal file transfers require further verification.
  • Raw combustion telemetry files were not found in the inspected public AWS mirror.
  • Live Gemini API reliability has not been consistently verified.
  • Gemini API timeouts have occurred during development.

FLAREX therefore reports its completed local testing separately from external service availability.

16. Scientific Research Areas Represented

The curated research database covers multiple areas relevant to combustion and fire-related research.

Flame Behavior

Research into flame structure, flame stability, flame shape, and environmental effects.

Solid Material Combustion

Research into the combustion behavior of solid materials, material geometry, and related physical processes.

Droplet Combustion

Research into the behavior of liquid fuel droplets and droplet combustion under different experimental conditions.

Smoke and Soot

Research into soot production, smoke characteristics, and particle behavior.

Material Flammability

Research into how materials respond to combustion-related conditions.

Airflow and Environmental Effects

Research into the influence of imposed airflow, pressure, oxygen concentration, and other experimental variables.

Battery Fire Research

Complementary research into lithium-ion battery fire behavior.

The battery research included in the curated material is terrestrial research. It should not be presented as direct microgravity experimental evidence.

These research areas provide a broader scientific context for exploring fire-related challenges in spacecraft environments.

17. Innovation and Differentiation

FLAREX combines several research capabilities that are often handled separately.

Its main contribution is the integration of scientific information discovery, evidence organization, dataset analysis, cross-study comparison, AI-assisted research, and reproducibility support within one environment.

Innovation 1: Evidence-Aware AI

AI-generated explanations are separated from documented scientific findings.

Innovation 2: Scientific Source Transparency

The platform distinguishes between a source link, retrieved metadata, a downloaded file, a validated dataset, and imported numerical data.

Innovation 3: Cross-Study Experimental Comparison

Experimental conditions are examined before studies are treated as directly comparable.

Innovation 4: Integrated Dataset Analysis

Users can import available data and perform statistical analysis within the platform.

Innovation 5: Research Gap Identification

Missing information and incomplete research coverage can be explored systematically.

Innovation 6: Reproducibility Tracking

Analytical runs can be associated with dataset identifiers, processing methods, and checksums.

Innovation 7: Scientific Audit

The platform includes validation and transparency checks designed to make weaknesses in the research workflow visible.

The combination of these capabilities makes FLAREX more than a conventional research-paper browsing interface.

18. Expected Impact

FLAREX aims to contribute to the accessibility and understanding of microgravity combustion research.

For Students

It can provide an organized environment for learning about space combustion experiments, scientific evidence, and data analysis.

For Researchers

It can support research discovery, source navigation, comparison of experimental conditions, and preliminary analysis of available datasets.

For Science Educators

It can help demonstrate how scientific investigations are documented, compared, and analyzed.

For Space Science Enthusiasts

It can provide a structured way to explore the science behind combustion in space.

For Future Research

The platform may support future work involving larger validated datasets, additional scientific investigations, and more advanced research comparison methods.

FLAREX is a research-support tool. Its outputs should not be used as operational fire-safety instructions or as a replacement for validated spacecraft engineering systems.

19. Future Development Roadmap

Future development will focus on improving the scientific completeness, reliability, and usability of FLAREX.

Phase 1: Expanded Scientific Data Access

  • Investigate additional public scientific datasets.
  • Improve source retrieval and file validation.
  • Add more verified experimental records.
  • Expand the range of supported scientific file formats.

Phase 2: Advanced Scientific Analysis

  • Improve statistical validation.
  • Expand cross-study comparison.
  • Add more scientific measurement metadata.
  • Improve uncertainty reporting.
  • Strengthen dataset quality checks.

Phase 3: AI Reliability

  • Improve retrieval quality.
  • Strengthen citation validation.
  • Expand scientific hallucination checks.
  • Improve fallback behavior when external AI services are unavailable.

Phase 4: Research Collaboration

  • Improve research workspace organization.
  • Support structured research notes.
  • Expand report generation.
  • Improve reproducibility documentation.

Phase 5: Scientific Coverage

  • Expand the investigation database.
  • Add more source-verified publications.
  • Improve coverage of smoke, soot, material combustion, and battery-related research.
  • Identify opportunities for future scientific collaboration.

These are proposed future development goals, not claims that the features have already been completed.

20. Limitations and Scientific Responsibility

FLAREX is designed around transparency, and its limitations are an important part of its documentation.

The current curated research database contains 16 research records. These are structured research metadata records, not 16 complete raw experimental datasets.

The availability of raw numerical data varies by investigation.

Some scientific records provide publication information or experimental descriptions without providing downloadable numerical measurements.

The public NASA PSI AWS mirror inspected during development did not expose the required combustion telemetry CSV files.

Authenticated or interactive PSI portal access remains a separate verification requirement.

Live Gemini API responses may experience timeouts or service interruptions.

Some comparisons may be limited by missing experimental variables or differences in measurement methods.

Statistical analysis can identify patterns and relationships, but it cannot independently establish causation.

AI-generated interpretations require careful examination and should not be treated as verified experimental results.

FLAREX therefore emphasizes source verification, evidence classification, reproducibility, and explicit communication of uncertainty.

21. Conclusion

FLAREX is an independent student-developed platform created to make microgravity combustion research easier to discover, understand, organize, and analyze.

It addresses an important scientific challenge: understanding how fire and combustion behave in space and how research information from different experiments can be connected responsibly.

By integrating NASA-related research discovery, scientific metadata organization, dataset ingestion, statistical analysis, experimental condition comparison, evidence intelligence, AI-assisted research, reproducibility tracking, and scientific auditing, FLAREX provides a unified environment for exploring space combustion science.

Its most important principle is that scientific reliability matters more than simply producing an answer.

A research platform should communicate what is known, what is supported by evidence, what has been calculated, what remains uncertain, and what information is still unavailable.

FLAREX is built around this principle.

FLAREX: Turning Microgravity Combustion Data into Space Fire Safety Insights.

22. Project Disclaimer

FLAREX is an independent student-developed project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

It is not an official NASA product, is not endorsed by NASA, and does not represent NASA's official scientific conclusions.

NASA names and scientific references are used to identify relevant research resources.

FLAREX does not replace certified spacecraft fire-safety systems, professional engineering analysis, or experimentally validated safety procedures.

AI-generated content is treated as research assistance and is distinguished from documented experimental findings and independently calculated statistical results.
